references.text: 5. Mosebok provides a parallel law regarding a man who lies with a virgin who is not betrothed. He must pay the bride price and marry her, and he may never divorce her.
The following verse explains what happens if the father refuses to give his daughter to the man - he must still pay the bride price for virgins.
Shechem offers to pay a bride price (mohar) for Dinah after lying with her, illustrating the practice of bride price mentioned in this verse.
Jacob offers seven years of service as a bride price for Rachel, showing how a bride price could be paid in labor.
Saul demands one hundred Philistine foreskins as a bride price for Michal, demonstrating variations in the bride price.
Deuteronomy 22:28 is the direct legal elaboration of Exodus 22:15, specifying the fine amount and the duration of the marriage.
Specifies the fine amount (50 shekels) and the rationale for the forced marriage resulting from violation of the law.
Contrasting cases illustrating the law's sharper distinction between a betrothed woman (death penalty) and an unbetrothed one (bride price/marriage).
